old: Its root described someone posted to watch from a higher vantage point — nothing religious about it at first.
The word simply meant 'overseer,' a sense the Tyndale Bible preserved by translating it plainly into English.
It shares its Greek root, epískopos, with the modern word 'episcopal.'
clues: This church title once meant simply an overseer, built from Greek words for 'over' and 'watcher,' and in ancient times it also named civil officials.
A senior Christian clergy member who oversees a whole diocese of parishes, ranking well above an ordinary priest and often wearing a tall pointed mitre.
It is also the chess piece that moves only diagonally, and a common family name taken straight from the church title.
